why: Alibaba's official approval in October 2026 meets 'officially approved imports of H200 chips by at least one Chinese firm'; the rung sets no quantity, and ByteDance's refusal cannot make rung 2 hold because rung 2 holds 'only when rung 1 does not'.
No firm is approved, and one firm's withdrawal with two requests still under review is neither a 'refusal of the requests' nor a 'withdrawal of it as a whole', so 'neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds'.

The November 2026 refusal of every request with the announcement that no H200 imports will be approved is 'an official Chinese refusal of the requests ... issued after 2026-07-08' that 'stands on 2027-01-31 with no firm approved'.

Every firm withdrawing in December 2026 with no request left reads as 'a formal abandonment or withdrawal of it as a whole after that day' that stands with no firm approved; this rests on taking the firms' withdrawal of all requests as a withdrawal of the event itself, which the rung does not say outright.

The October 2026 approval meets 'on or before 2027-01-31 Chinese authorities have officially approved imports ... by at least one Chinese firm'; rung 1 has no word that the approval must still stand (only rung 2 says 'stands'), so the December revocation does not undo it, though a reader who takes 'have approved' as the state on the due day would not pick rung 1.
With no official announcement of any kind there is no official approval and no 'official Chinese refusal' or 'prohibition ... issued after 2026-07-08', so 'neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds'.
No firm is approved, and the unchanged restriction dates from before July 2026, so it is not one 'issued after 2026-07-08' nor a decision 'taken after 2026-07-08'; 'neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds'.

A licensing rule for AI-chip shipments to third countries published in the Federal Register in November 2026 meets 'has adopted a binding restriction, a licensing rule or any other, on advanced AI-chip shipments to third countries beyond its May 2026 guidance', reading a published rule that is not called proposed as adopted.

Nothing 'has adopted', and withdrawing one proposed rule while another is open for comment is neither an announcement 'that it will adopt no such restriction' nor a 'withdrawal of it as a whole', so 'neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds'.

The November 2026 announcement that it will not go beyond the May guidance, with the only proposal withdrawn and nothing changed since, is 'an announcement by the Commerce Department, made after 2026-07-14, that it will adopt no such restriction' that 'stands on 2027-01-31'.

The binding licensing rule adopted in September 2026 (taken to be the kind the question asks about) meets 'on or before 2027-01-31 the Commerce Department has adopted a binding restriction'; rung 1 has no word that the rule must still be in force, so the rescission of 2027-01-15 does not undo it, though a reader who takes 'has adopted' as the state on the due day would not pick rung 1.
With no proposal, no announcement and the guidance as it was, nothing 'has adopted' and there is no announcement 'that it will adopt no such restriction', so 'neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds'.

The words 'beyond its May 2026 guidance' exclude restrictions adopted in 2025 before that guidance, and nothing has been adopted or announced since, so 'neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds'; rung 1 names no start day of its own, so this rests wholly on reading 'beyond' as something added on top of the guidance.
No sale is shown, and the August 2026 prohibition was lifted in December so it does not meet 'stands on 2027-01-31'; 'neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds'.

The August 2026 prohibition is 'a formal Chinese prohibition on purchases ... imposed after 2026-07-02' that is in force and so 'stands on 2027-01-31', with no sale made; an announced review does not lift it.

Revenue from H200 sales to a Chinese customer disclosed in the Form 10-Q published in November 2026 meets 'Nvidia has made H200 sales to customers in China, as shown by Nvidia's disclosures ... published on or before that day'.
A permission is not a sale, so nothing shows that 'Nvidia has made H200 sales', and no prohibition or 'decision against the event' stands; 'neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds'.
No sale was made, and the bar already in place in June 2026 is not a prohibition 'imposed after 2026-07-02' nor a decision 'taken after 2026-07-02'; 'neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds'.
Closing in June 2027 meets 'Nvidia has completed the acquisition of Hugging Face on or before 2028-03-05'; the rung sets no price.

The agreement's expiry in January 2028 with both companies confirming they will not go on is 'a termination of the acquisition announced by Nvidia or Hugging Face after 2026-09-05' (or 'a formal abandonment ... of it as a whole') that 'stands on 2028-03-05', and the deal was not completed.

A suit to block that is still in court is not yet 'a regulator's block' nor any 'decision against the event', the deal has not closed and neither company has ended it, so 'neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds'.

The court's block of December 2027 is 'any other decision against the event of rung 1 as a whole taken after 2026-09-05' and, not being overturned, 'stands on 2028-03-05'; this rests on reading a block under a pending appeal as still standing, which the rung does not say outright.
The deal has not closed, and moving the latest closing date to September 2028 is neither a 'termination', a 'block' nor an 'abandonment or withdrawal', so 'neither rung 1 nor rung 2 holds'.
